\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{مخفر} (makhfar)}{مخفر (makhfar)}]{\ar{مخفر} (makhfar) — a police station}

\label{lesson:AR-C451-makhfar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a line of people, then the Arabic for to apply.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{مخفر}}
\textbf{\ar{مخفر}} — \emph{makhfar} — \textquotedblleft{}a police station\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{ذهب} \ar{الرجل} \ar{إلى} \ar{المخفر} \ar{بعد} \ar{الحادث}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dhahaba ar-rajul ilā al-makhfar baʿda al-ḥādith.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The man went to the police station after the accident.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{مخفر}} (\emph{makhfar}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{kh-f-r}, \textquotedblleft{}to guard, to protect\textquotedblright{} (Lane). The pattern \emph{mafʿal} makes it a guard post.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{makhfar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{makhfar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dhahaba ar-rajul ilā al-makhfar baʿda al-ḥādith.} — The man went to the police station after the accident.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a line of people, then the Arabic for to apply, then say \emph{makhfar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{مخفر} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A police station\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{مكتبة} (maktaba)}{مكتبة (maktaba)}]{\ar{مكتبة} (maktaba) — a library; a bookshop}

\label{lesson:AR-C451-maktaba}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to apply, then the Arabic for a police station.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{مكتبة}}
\textbf{\ar{مكتبة}} — \emph{maktaba} — \textquotedblleft{}a library; a bookshop\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{قرأت} \ar{في} \ar{المكتبة} \ar{حتى} \ar{المساء}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{qaraʾtu fī al-maktaba ḥattā al-masāʾ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I read in the library until the evening.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{مكتبة}} (\emph{maktaba}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{k-t-b}, \textquotedblleft{}to write\textquotedblright{} (Lane). The pattern \emph{mafʿala} makes it the place of books.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to apply, then the Arabic for a police station, then say \emph{maktaba} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{استفسر} (istafsara)}{استفسر (istafsara)}]{\ar{استفسر} (istafsara) — to enquire}

\label{lesson:AR-C451-istafsara}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a police station, then the Arabic for a library.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{استفسر}}
\textbf{\ar{استفسر}} — \emph{istafsara} — \textquotedblleft{}to enquire\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{استفسر} \ar{أبي} \ar{عن} \ar{الحافلة} \ar{الأخيرة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{istafsara abī ʿan al-ḥāfila al-akhīra.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My father enquired about the last bus.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يستفسر}, \emph{yastafsir}.

It takes \emph{ʿan}: \emph{istafsara ʿan}, \textquotedblleft{}to ask about\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{استفسر}} (\emph{istafsara}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{f-s-r}, \textquotedblleft{}to explain\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form X, \textquotedblleft{}to ask for an explanation\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{istafsara}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a police station, then the Arabic for a library, then say \emph{istafsara} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{راجع} (rājaʿa)}{راجع (rājaʿa)}]{\ar{راجع} (rājaʿa) — to check over; to go back to (an office)}

\label{lesson:AR-C451-rajaa-check}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a library, then the Arabic for to enquire.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{راجع}}
\textbf{\ar{راجع}} — \emph{rājaʿa} — \textquotedblleft{}to check over; to go back to (an office)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{راجعت} \ar{الموظفة} \ar{الأوراق}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{rājaʿat al-muwaẓẓafa al-awrāq.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The clerk checked over the papers.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يراجع}, \emph{yurājiʿ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{راجع}} (\emph{rājaʿa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{r-j-ʿ}, \textquotedblleft{}to return\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form III, \textquotedblleft{}to go back over\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{حظر} (ḥaẓara)}{حظر (ḥaẓara)}]{\ar{حظر} (ḥaẓara) — to ban}

\label{lesson:AR-C451-hazara}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to enquire, then the Arabic for to check over.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{حظر}}
\textbf{\ar{حظر}} — \emph{ḥaẓara} — \textquotedblleft{}to ban\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{حظرت} \ar{البلدية} \ar{السيارات} \ar{في} \ar{وسط} \ar{المدينة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ḥaẓarat al-baladiyya as-sayyārāt fī wasaṭ al-madīna.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The town hall banned cars in the city centre.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يحظر}, \emph{yaḥẓur}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{حظر}} (\emph{ḥaẓara}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ḥ-ẓ-r}, \textquotedblleft{}to forbid; to fence in\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is the plain verb.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}
